rankings-bent-for-money.why: I read the WilmerHale report in full. It establishes the bending: data altered in two editions for four countries, by an investigation the Bank itself commissioned. The money link is firm for China - the Senior Director for DEC took Georgieva's thanks for doing his 'bit for multilateralism' and read it as not angering China during the capital increase negotiations - and the report's conclusion on Saudi Arabia is that the change was 'likely' an effort to reward the country for its role in the Bank community 'including its significant and ongoing RAS projects'. Two editions and two paying or capital-contributing countries is the practice, not one episode. Two qualifications the reviewer did not weigh: the Saudi change's first stated consideration is an instruction to find a way to drop Jordan from the Top Improvers list, with the RAS motive one of three listed factors; and Azerbaijan's data was cut on Djankov's own disbelief and apparent personal animus, with no money in it. The report also records employees' concern that RAS 'can lead to the impression of a pay-to-play scheme' - an impression recorded, not a finding.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: WilmerHale report, 15 Sep 2021, paras 14-25 (China, Saudi/UAE, Azerbaijan) and 31-36 (motive), read in full

rankings-bent-for-money.what_would_change_my_mind: If the owner reads the title's 'for countries with money to give' as covering all four countries, Azerbaijan breaks it and the verdict falls to overclaimed. A Bank publication of the full original-and-final data with each change's requester could also show the two found cases were outliers.

private-equity-with-development-money.why: The title asserts only the channel, and the channel is published by the institutions and audited by a statutory body. I opened the ICAI review: health was 7 per cent of CDC's portfolio at end-2017, 258.8 million pounds, and 17 per cent of new investments from 2012 to Q3 2017 went through funds rather than direct equity or debt. ICAI also records that for an Indian healthcare fund the investment papers did not consider which groups would benefit, that CDC later said the funded services had largely reached those on above-average incomes, and that papers for more than three-quarters of the sample ignored the question. So documented is the right verdict on the test as written. I would flag to the owner that this is the weakest of the six as a page change: the title asserts something nobody disputes, and everything the story is actually about - fees, fraud, patients priced out - stays suspected, so graduating it as written would put a dry, near-tautological pattern beside the thirteen.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: ICAI performance review of CDC, Mar 2019, read for paras 4.11-4.12, Figure 12 and paras 4.90-4.92

private-equity-with-development-money.what_would_change_my_mind: Nothing on the facts. If the owner's rule is that a pattern must assert something a reader could doubt, then this is better rewritten around a contested claim than promoted.

companies-pay-armed-groups.why: Documented, and on firmer ground than the reviewer had. The DOJ release carries every figure in paragraph 1: over 100 payments totalling over $1.7 million from 1997 to 4 Feb 2004 through Banadex, booked as 'security payments', 50 payments of over $825,000 after the AUC was designated, 20 payments of over $300,000 after Chiquita disclosed to the Justice Department, a $25 million fine, and the finding that Chiquita never received any actual security services. For Freeport I could not read the 10-K body, but EDGAR full-text search returns the exact phrase 'support costs for government-provided security' in nine consecutive Freeport 10-Ks, FY2017 through FY2025, including the accession the reviewer cited. A payment practice a company has restated in every annual report for nine years is not an exposed scandal; it is ordinary disclosed business. Two guilty pleas plus that settle the plural claim in the title. Two things to fix before anything moves: the conviction line's 'routinely' is not documented and should go, and the DOJ release says the AUC demanded the payments, that Castano implied failure could bring physical harm to Banadex personnel and property, and that Chiquita represented the payments as made under threat of violence - the entry gives none of that, and HYP's fairness rule wants it.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: DOJ release 07-161, 19 Mar 2007, read in full including the outside-counsel advice and the post-disclosure payments
SEC EDGAR full-text search: 9 hits, all Freeport 10-Ks for FY2017-FY2025 (CIK 0000831259), including 0000831259-26-000012:fcx-20251231.htm

companies-pay-armed-groups.what_would_change_my_mind: If the owner wants the title to carry 'routinely', it becomes overclaimed, because no disclosure requirement exists and so no count does. Reading Chiquita's payments as pure extortion rather than protection buying would also narrow it.

water-handed-to-companies.why: Documented at the portfolio level, and only there. The IEG evaluation states it in its own words: 'Thirteen percent of projects dealing with urban WSS aimed to introduce PSP. Seventy of these projects have closed, and 46 had managed to involve the private sector as planned', with Bolivia cancelling all its contracts and Turkey and Venezuela terminating early, and the international private sector focusing on large and medium-size cities while local firms took rural work. That is the lender designing projects to bring foreign operators into city water, counted across its own portfolio, which is the title read as a programme. It is not a per-city claim about advice, and the entry's own second case contradicts one: the 1998 Jabotabek completion report says the privatisation of PAM JAYA's operations was 'parallel to but facilitated by the Project' and in the same sentence that it 'was not envisaged by GOI and the Bank at appraisal', and at paragraph 28 that in the late 1980s 'had GOI proposed a PSP option, it would have most likely been turned down by the Bank'. Cochabamba's conditioned loan still rests on the Democracy Center, not on a lender document.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: IEG, Water and Development, 30 Jun 2010, private-sector-participation chapter read
World Bank ICR, Second Jabotabek Urban Development Project, 23 Jun 1998, paras xii, 28 and 32

water-handed-to-companies.what_would_change_my_mind: If 'on the lenders' advice' is read as a claim about each city, this is overclaimed, and the reviewer's own fallback title - city water handed to private companies in projects the World Bank designed to bring them in - is the safer one. A Bank document conditioning the Cochabamba loan on privatisation would settle the per-city reading the other way.

secret-loans-banks-traders.why: Documented, just past the single-episode bar. The FCA final notice is a regulator's finding and its wording checks out: Mozambique was 'only willing to represent in general terms that it had complied with its IMF obligations rather than undertake to inform the IMF of the loans in question', a senior official refused a provision requiring notification, a Credit Suisse managing director said that if Mozambique did not want to notify 'we can live without it, as [there is] no legal risk to us', and in January 2014 the purported purpose of the First Loan 'was still not public knowledge'. The Bank's own board paper then generalises: 'There have been several recent cases of hidden debt among IDA countries', naming Congo's oil-trader prefinancing contracts undisclosed to the debt management office for over two years, Togo's prefinanced debt at 7 per cent of GDP, and Mozambique's 2013 and 2014 guarantees of $1.15 billion 'not disclosed to the debt management staff and the public'. One caveat the reviewer should have carried: of the Bank's three sovereigns only Congo names an arranger type and Togo names none, so the banks-and-traders element rests on Credit Suisse, Congo's oil traders and Glencore in Chad rather than on the box alone.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: FCA Final Notice to Credit Suisse, 19 Oct 2021, read for the 147,190,200 pound penalty and paras 4.18-4.19 and 2.x findings
World Bank, Debt Vulnerabilities in IDA Countries, 4 Oct 2018, Box 3 'Hidden Debt' read in full

secret-loans-banks-traders.what_would_change_my_mind: Reading the Bank's box as three instances rather than a practice drops this to overclaimed. The conviction line's 'routine' stays unsupported either way: there is no creditor-side count for Western banks and traders of the kind AidData made for Chinese lenders.

ratings-that-punish-relief.why: The weakest of the six, and I agree only because the actions themselves are a documentary record across several countries and agencies. What I could open: the African Peer Review Mechanism's statement that 'The key driver of Ethiopia's rating downgrade is the announcement by the government' that it would use the Common Framework, two notches B to CCC on 9 February 2021 while Moody's and S&P still had B2 and B; the UNDP brief recommending that an appeal for relief 'should not lead to rating downgrades'; and Oxfam's July 2020 brief recording that 'In May, Moody's put Ethiopia's rating on review following its request to join the DSSI', with Pakistan under review on 14 May for the same reason, footnoted to Moody's own press release. Nobody in this round opened an agency's own notice, which is the gap. Two things the entry must carry before it moves: the figure defect below, and the counter-evidence in the same Oxfam brief - Moody's said DSSI relief on bilateral debt could ease funding pressures and possibly help ratings, and Fitch and S&P supported countries joining to the extent it applied only to bilateral debt. The punishment attaches to private-creditor involvement, which is narrower and more interesting than the title.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: APRM statement, 11 Feb 2021, read in full
UNDP policy brief, Apr 2023, sample tables and recommendations read
Oxfam, Passing the Buck on Debt Relief, Jul 2020, section on credit agencies' mixed signals

ratings-that-punish-relief.what_would_change_my_mind: If the owner holds to REVIEW42's rule that a promotion needs a document opened that is the finding itself, this is not there yet: the key-driver claim is an interested party's reading of Fitch, and Fitch, Moody's and S&P notices are all walled. Fitch's own 9 Feb 2021 action commentary would settle it either way.

vulture-funds.why: The overlap is real. I read holdout-funds-rich-courts out of base.html: it already carries ECB WP 2135's 158 cases against 34 sovereigns, 130 in US courts, 79 of 148 known-creditor cases filed by funds, 65 per cent since 2000 from distressed debt funds, the paper's own description of buying at a discount and suing for full repayment, Elliott v Peru, Argentina's 182 suits and over $10 billion paid to holdouts in 2016, seizure attempts in 56 per cent of fund cases, and the New York bills. The entry's core adds nothing to that. What is genuinely left over is the poor-country cut, which is what the entry's title is actually about and which the ECB paper does not isolate: the UN independent expert's 2010 report of 54 cases by commercial creditors against 12 heavily indebted poor countries from 1998 to 2008, Donegal v Zambia while Zambia was receiving relief, the ARA Libertad seizure, and the UK's 2010 Act and Belgium's 2015 law - I checked base.html and the pattern carries none of those four. Hamilton Reserve v Sri Lanka is not a leftover: who-owns-the-debt already carries it.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: window.PATS, holdout-funds-rich-courts and who-owns-the-debt read in full, and searched for Donegal, Libertad, Belgium and 42.5

vulture-funds.what_would_change_my_mind: Nothing on the duplication. If the owner would rather keep a suspicion than merge, the only open part is whether the business depends on other creditors granting relief, since purchase prices are not disclosed.

bondholders-block-debt-relief.why: Duplicate on the core, but the reviewer's inventory of the existing pattern is wrong in one place. who-owns-the-debt does carry BlackRock as Zambia's largest known holder with $220 million, the $165 million purchase estimate, the 110 per cent profit figure, BlackRock's replies, and that all of Zambia's private lenders except Intesa Sanpaolo refused the September 2020 suspension request - so paragraph 1 is mostly restatement. It does not carry the missed $42.5 million payment: I searched the pattern text and the figure is not there. Leftover, as the reviewer says: the scheme-wide DSSI record, the Debt Justice five-country $20 to $30 billion estimate, the 2024 deal and the 2021 budget comparison. The leftover is itself unverified - the reviewer opened no document for this entry and both World Bank DSSI pages load their figures by script - so a merge should not carry the $12.9 billion and one-private-creditor claims until someone opens a document that states them.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: window.PATS, who-owns-the-debt read in full and searched for 42.5 and 12.9

bondholders-block-debt-relief.what_would_change_my_mind: A document establishing that the scheme-wide refusal is the general pattern rather than Zambia's story repeated would make the leftover big enough to stand on its own rather than merge.

development-money-through-tax-havens.why: Duplicate, yes - offshore-routing-lost-tax already carries UNCTAD's $100 billion, the IMF economists' nearly 40 per cent of FDI through empty companies, Mauritius among the ten hosts and Senegal's $257 million treaty termination, which is the entry's paragraph 2. But I do not agree with the reviewer on the leftover. The reviewer says the IFC client count 'reads as documented' and belongs beside the existing pattern. On what has actually been opened it does not meet REVIEW42's bar: it is an advocacy group's count of IFC disclosures, known here through an Oxfam press release and the Bretton Woods Project, with the briefing itself opening for nobody in this round. And the claim that carries the weight - that the IFC disputed the reading but not the numbers - is not in either document: I read the Bretton Woods Project article in full and it carries no IFC response at all, only Jim Yong Kim saying moving state assets to tax havens 'can have a tremendous negative effect on our mission'. The IFC investments dataset redirects to a script-built page, so the count cannot yet be reproduced from the lender's own data.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: Bretton Woods Project, 23 Sep 2016, read in full - carries the 51-of-68 count and Kim's statement, no IFC reply
window.PATS, offshore-routing-lost-tax read in full and searched for IFC

development-money-through-tax-havens.what_would_change_my_mind: Reproducing the 51-of-68 count from IFC's own published disclosures, or opening an IFC response that contests the reading and not the numbers, would make the leftover documented and I would then agree it belongs beside the existing pattern.

private-courts-for-investors.why: Agreed, and for the reason the reviewer gives: as written the title asserts the existence and power of investor-state tribunals, which nothing disputes, and the documented core is already company-sued-the-state. I checked that pattern in base.html: it lists claims and awards case by case, names ICSID as one of the five organizations of the World Bank Group, carries Occidental's $980 million, and records that in Cochabamba the World Bank's president named the presiding arbitrator. It does not carry Tethyan or Reko Diq or the 1,332-case count, so those widen it. The leftover the reviewer names - fifteen arbitrators deciding most cases, board seats, double-hatting, regulatory chill - is the only part still open, and it is contested in print and unmeasured, so it cannot graduate either; it is what a retitled suspicion would have to assert.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: window.PATS, company-sued-the-state read in full and searched for Tethyan, Reko, Occidental, 1,332 and arbitrator

private-courts-for-investors.what_would_change_my_mind: A measured study of claims withdrawn or laws dropped after a threatened claim would turn the leftover into something that could stand as a documented pattern of its own.

aid-cover-for-spies.why: Correctly scoped, and the conviction line - four cases on the record, each exposed by accident, with continuation the suspicion - matches what the record carries. The best document here is a senator's 1992 release of a GAO report, which is a characterisation, not an official finding that aid was used as cover; Australia has never admitted the Dili bugging; USAID says ZunZuneo was not covert. One standing defect, unfixed since the 15 November check and reported again by reviewer A: the Office of Public Safety paragraph still rests on Wikipedia for the 1,500 advisers in at least 52 countries and for Byron Engle, when the entry's own Federation of American Scientists source carries the Congressional Record and the GAO figures.
aid-cover-for-spies.what_would_change_my_mind: An official declassified record of a standing programme of intelligence work under aid cover after 1974, or the USAID inspector general's 2014 ZunZuneo review.

ports-that-become-naval-bases.why: Correctly scoped. The title is hedged with 'may' and the conviction line matches: one base, one facility hosting warships, and a researched shortlist that its own authors present as inference. That is the textbook case of the pieces being documented and the join not.
ports-that-become-naval-bases.what_would_change_my_mind: Publication of the concession or loan contracts for a shortlisted port showing naval use contemplated at the time of lending.

pension-funds-buy-up-farmland.why: Correctly scoped, and the conviction line is honest where it matters: it calls the Incra report preliminary and describes the Bahia court as freezing a deed rather than ruling, which is what the round 28 check corrected. The verdict is right. Process note rather than classification: the reviewer recorded no document opened for this entry, so the conviction was accepted rather than checked, which REVIEW42 permits for a suspicion but which leaves this the least examined of the five.
pension-funds-buy-up-farmland.what_would_change_my_mind: A concluded Brazilian proceeding, or a published farm-level register of pension fund and endowment holdings, would move it.

lenders-expect-the-riots.why: Correctly scoped. The conviction line puts the weight on a leaked strategy, a protest count and a study linking adjustment lending to repression, and leaves the planning as the suspicion, which is where the record leaves it. The one thing the conviction does not acknowledge is that the size of the measured effect is still being re-estimated, which the reviewer found in the paper it opened; that is a nuance for the story, not a reason to reclassify.
lenders-expect-the-riots.what_would_change_my_mind: A programme document whose risk section forecasts unrest before a price rise, with a record of whether the programme changed - the reviewer is right that this count is doable from published staff reports and nobody has done it.

rescue-money-timed-for-elections.why: Correctly scoped. The conviction line claims only three rescues arriving before elections, one reported official admission and one president's public condition, and leaves regularity as the suspicion - it does not lean on the academic result, which is right, because the reviewer found the Dreher, Marchesi and Vreeland finding is about inflation forecasts rather than when money arrives and is significant in the GMM estimates but not in the OLS marginal effects. The story's third paragraph does lean on it, which is a story defect for a later pass, not a classification problem.
rescue-money-timed-for-elections.what_would_change_my_mind: A count across all IMF programmes of approvals and disbursements in the months before elections against voting alignment, or the US Treasury's voting instructions for 1996 Russia and 2018 Argentina.

bribes-built-into-financed-contracts.why: Agreed that the title overclaims - nothing shows the bribe is priced into the contract and repaid by the borrower with interest. But the narrower title concedes too little, and I verified why: I opened the FY2024 Sanctions System Data Companion and the corruption-ground sanctions are there firm by firm - M/S Gul Construction (Pakistan, corruption and fraud), BETS Consulting Services (Bangladesh), Marseille for Engineering & Trading (Iraq), Ernst & Young LLP (Kenya, on a Somalia project), TPF Getinsa Euroestudios (Spain, on a Viet Nam project) - and the Bank publishes a new set every year. With the Lesotho convictions and the Siemens debarment, 'bribes paid to win the contracts that development loans finance' is itself documented, so the right action is graduate under the narrower title, not keep as a suspicion. One correction to the reviewer: TPF Getinsa received conditional non-debarment, not a debarment, so the count of six debarments on corruption grounds is one too many.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: World Bank Group Sanctions System Data Companion FY2024, debarment tables read for the corruption grounds

bribes-built-into-financed-contracts.what_would_change_my_mind: If the owner holds that one year of debarment tables plus two convictions is still a set of instances, the narrower claim stays suspected too.

loans-cut-off-to-topple-governments.why: Agreed on the verdict - the toppling purpose is documented for Chile and not for the other cases, so the plural title overclaims. But the narrower title concedes too much by dropping the purpose entirely, and I checked the primary myself. The Senate report sets out NSDM 93 of November 1970 in its own words: 'The U.S. would use its predominant position in international financial institutions to dry up the flow of new multilateral credit or other financial assistance', with IDB loans falling from $46 million in 1970 to $2 million in 1972, no new World Bank loans between 1970 and 1973, and Helms's notes from the 15 September 1970 meeting that initiated Track II reading 'Make the economy scream.' A narrower title should keep that: lending blocked through the banks the West controls, and in Chile as part of an effort to bring the government down. The same report also holds counter-evidence the entry should carry - the IMF extended Chile about $90 million during 1971 and 1972.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: Senate Select Committee, Covert Action in Chile 1963-1973, section on the instruments of US economic policy and Table II

loans-cut-off-to-topple-governments.what_would_change_my_mind: If Nicaragua 1985 or Haiti 2001 turned out to have a documented toppling purpose as well, the full title would be documented.

poor-countries-take-the-poison.why: Agreed on the verdict: the selection in the title rests mainly on the 1991 memo, which was a memo and not a decision, and which both the man who signed it and the man who wrote it say was sarcasm - the entry already says so, which is the fairness rule being met. But the narrower title concedes too much. 'Ends up in' drops the deliberateness that the Probo Koala record does carry: the waste was offered in Amsterdam and taken back on board, then disposed of in Abidjan for about $17,000, and a Dutch court fined Trafigura for concealing how dangerous it was. A narrower title should keep the sequence - hazardous waste exported to poor countries after richer ports refused it, for a fraction of the price - rather than retreat to a passive statement about where waste ends up.
poor-countries-take-the-poison.what_would_change_my_mind: A study matching Basel Convention export reports against receiving countries' wages and treatment capacity, which the entry itself names, would decide whether the selection is the rule.

banks-that-bank-the-looters.why: Agreed, and I verified the pivot. The Senate report's own words, twice, are that Riggs 'turned a blind eye to evidence suggesting the bank was handling the proceeds of foreign corruption', and the plea was for failing to report suspicious transactions, so 'knowingly' in the title is not the Senate's finding. The report does record affirmative help - Riggs opened multiple personal accounts for the president, his wife and other relatives, helped establish offshore shell corporations for the president and his sons, and facilitated nearly $13 million in cash deposits between 2000 and 2002 - so knowledge is close for that one bank, which is what the reviewer says. The narrower title is well judged.

documents_i_opened.what_it_is: Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, Jul 2004, Riggs case study - executive summary and findings on the Equatorial Guinea accounts

banks-that-bank-the-looters.what_would_change_my_mind: A regulator's or court's finding that a bank knew it was holding stolen state money, at more than one bank, would carry the title as written.
